{{nihongo|'''Okataka Shrine'''|岡高神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

===Enshrined deities===
It enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005|lt=Sugawara no Michizane-kō}} (すがわらみちざねこう) and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}.

===Shrine crest===
Star-plum-bowl crest

===History===
In year 3 of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}} ({{ill|459|Q30500|qid=Q30500}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gamō no Inagi Samamaro}} first enshrined {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} on Senjōo-dake, 2 km east of the current site; in {{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}} 13 ({{ill|685|Q33480|qid=Q33480}}), it was moved to the current otabisho. In {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}} 1 ({{ill|851|Q29966|qid=Q29966}}), {{ill|Ono no Takamura|Q1139928|qid=Q1139928}} built shrine buildings at the current site and called it Okamoto Shrine. At that time this area was Okamoto-gō of Asai District. During syncretic times, there was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Okatakayama Jingū-ji}}. In the Sengoku period, clergy avoided {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}}’s temple-shrine burnings by inviting from Kyoto’s {{ill|Kitano Tenmangū|Q662176|qid=Q662176}}, having heard that his father Nobuhide revered {{ill|Tenmangū|Q798838|qid=Q798838}}, and called it Okataka Tenjin.
From early Meiji it became Okataka Shrine; in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 9 ({{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}}) it became {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}, and in Meiji 17 ({{ill|1884|Q7819|qid=Q7819}}) it became {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

As the sōsha of 15 villages of Shimokusano-shō, it was deeply revered. In droughts, rain prayers were held, choosing among taiko dance, yuno-hana, and tōmyō rites; when prayers were fulfilled, a thanksgiving taiko dance by all 15 villages was dedicated. This rain-prayer custom continued until before the war; now it has ceased, with three taiko dance preservation groups remaining.

The main sanctuary was built in {{ill|Shōtoku (era)|Q1193848|qid=Q1193848|lt=Shōtoku}} 6 ({{ill|1716|Q6892|qid=Q6892}}) by Ubahuchi Jirosuke (Kaodo Village) as nagare-zukuri with chidori-karahafu. The worship hall was completed in Meiji 21 by master builder {{ill|Itō Heizaemon IX|Q17193360|qid=Q17193360|lt=Itō Heizaemon Morimichi}} of {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}} as an irimoyao-zukuri, cypress-bark roof, 4-ken frontage by 3-ken depth.
The middle gate and corridor fence were built in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 5 ({{ill|1930|Q18787|qid=Q18787}}), and the shrine office was rebuilt in {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 3 ({{ill|1991|Q2062|qid=Q2062}}) as an imperial enthronement commemorative project.
